review_candidates.description: Imagine having the power to stress-test an entire power grid against a hurricane or thunderstorm before the clouds even gather. That is the reality we are creating at Neara. We use advanced machine learning to create engineering-grade, physics enabled digital twins of electricity grids across four continents, this helps asset owners understand their biggest challenges and bring the most viable solutions to life across millions of kilometres of infrastructure. By simulating extreme weather and structural stress at a network-wide scale, we empower the world’s largest utilities to pinpoint risks, optimise investments and build a more resilient global energy future. Our team is a collection of brilliant minds who are fanatical about making a tangible difference in the real world, utilising AI and machine learning to accelerate everything from data classification to complex scenario analysis. We have built a special culture where innovation thrives because everyone owns the mission and we need smart, creative people to help us scale this impact to every corner of the globe. Director, Key Accounts We're seeking a driven, dynamic, and strategic commercial leader to drive growth across our key accounts in Europe. This is a hands-on, high-impact player-coach role focused predominantly on personal account execution paired with informal team leadership and commercial mentoring. To succeed in this role, you will need a consultative mindset, excellent communication skills, and knowledge of the utilities industry. You will also need a proven track record of commercial execution across large, multi-year, multi-faceted contracts, and experience leading or mentoring a customer-facing team. What You'll Do Personally own and grow relationships with a portfolio of our most strategic accounts, serving as the senior commercial relationship owner and executive point of contact. Develop and deliver expansion plans across assigned key accounts to execute against business metrics and revenue goals. Coach the team on account strategy, executive engagement, and commercial execution on complex, multi-year contracts. Identify new workflow improvements and use-case opportunities, helping to upskill the broader customer-facing team in commercial best practices. Collaborate with Customer Success Operations, Customer Value Architects, and Product on overall account strategy and execution. Develop processes to scale the Key Account Management function as Neara's European business grows. Co-present with utilities at key conferences and events across Europe, helping elevate Neara’s market presence. Report on account performance, pipeline, and expansion opportunities to senior leadership. Who You Are Demonstrated history of personally managing and expanding enterprise-level accounts within complex technical or SaaS environments, ideally operating as a Director of Key Accounts, Key Account Manager, Director of Sales, Client Partner, or in a similar enterprise role. Domain exposure to the utilities sector or a similarly complex, technical, infrastructure-heavy industry is highly desirable. Experience leading, managing, or mentoring Account Managers or Customer Success Managers, ideally in a player-coach capacity. Experience in strategic sales, management consulting, or tech-enabled enterprise environments. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to navigate executive dynamics and foster a collaborative, customer-centric culture internally. Fluent in English (required); additional European languages are a plus. What We Are Offering You Competitive salary + commission structure. Significant development opportunities with scope for lateral and upward movement in a high-growth company. Highly meritocratic, non-bureaucratic, and low-ego work culture. The opportunity to play a direct, critical role in expanding Neara’s footprint across Europe’s largest utilities to solve real-world infrastructure problems. Enjoy the opportunity to work across multiple business areas and build relationships with key internal and external stakeholders. Compensation Range: £110K - £120K

review_candidates.description: Title: Director, Policy and Research Department: Strategy, and Policy Research Reporting to: Senior Director, Policy and Research Compensation: CAD102K - CAD131K Employment: Full Time Location: Remote - Canada (The team is primarily based in Ontario; candidates located in Ontario are encouraged to apply)   Who We Are:     World Education Services (WES) is a non-profit social enterprise that supports the educational, economic, and social inclusion of immigrants, refugees, and international students. For 50 years, WES has set the standard for international academic credential evaluation, supporting millions of people as they seek to achieve their academic and professional goals. Through decades of experience as a leader in global education, WES has developed a wide range of tools to pursue social impact at scale. From evaluating academic credentials to shaping policy, designing programs, and providing philanthropic funding, we partner with a diverse set of organizations, leaders, and networks to uplift individuals and drive systems change. Together with its partners, WES enables people to learn, work, and thrive in new places. For more information about WES, please visit our website at www.WES.org.         About the Opportunity: The Director, Policy and Research provides strategic leadership in advancing WES Canada's policy, research, and advocacy agenda. Working closely with the Senior Director, Strategy and Policy Research, the Director leads major policy initiatives, develops evidence-based policy positions, manages strategic research, and cultivates high-impact partnerships that strengthen WES's influence across Canada's immigration and workforce development. The Director leads complex cross-functional initiatives that advance WES Canada's strategic priorities. This role combines senior policy leadership with hands-on technical research capability, including the design and execution of applied economic research on immigration, economics, and labour market outcomes. The Director provides leadership to policy staff, consultants, and project teams while fostering collaboration across WES departments to strengthen organizational impact and thought leadership. The role is responsible for translating emerging policy trends and research into organizational strategy, supporting executive decision making, and representing WES externally with governments, business associations, sector partners, and other stakeholders. What You'll Do: Policy Leadership and Strategic Influence (35%) Apply rigorous economic and quantitative analysis, including econometric evidence on immigration and labour market outcomes to strengthen the empirical foundation of WES policy positions. Lead the development of policy positions, strategic analysis, consultation submissions, and advocacy strategies aligned with WES Canada's priorities. Identify emerging immigration, labour market, education, and workforce policy trends and assess strategic implications for WES. Lead complex policy research projects that support evidence-informed organizational decision making. Provide strategic advice to senior leadership regarding policy risks, opportunities, and emerging issues. Develop policy frameworks and recommendations that strengthen WES's influence with governments and sector partners. Represent WES in external policy forums, advisory committees, and stakeholder consultations. Lead the preparation of executive briefing materials, policy papers, presentations, and strategic reports. Research, Thought Leadership and Strategic Partnerships (30%) Design and lead applied economic research on immigration and workforce integration, including econometric and quantitative studies related to immigration policy or economic issues, credential recognition, and labour market outcomes. Direct strategic research initiatives that support WES Canada's public policy, advocacy, and systems change objectives. Build and steward the team’s technical research capacity, including research design, quantitative methods, data acquisition, analytical tooling, and quality assurance standards for all empirical economic-focused work. Build and maintain senior relationships with governments, business associations, post-secondary institutions, regulatory bodies, employers, and sector organizations. Identify opportunities for collaborative research, policy development, and strategic partnerships that advance WES priorities. Lead the development and dissemination of thought leadership publications, policy briefs, and research reports. Provide strategic oversight of external research partnerships and ensure research quality and alignment with organizational priorities. Represent WES as a recognized subject matter expert through speaking engagements, conferences, and stakeholder meetings. Strategy, Governance and Organizational Leadership (20%) Lead strategic planning initiatives that support implementation of WES Canada's strategic priorities as it relates to policy, research, and the advocacy agenda. Direct cross-functional projects involving multiple departments and external stakeholders. Lead strategic environmental scanning and scenario planning activities to inform executive decision making. Support organizational governance through development of board materials, executive briefings, dashboards, and performance reporting. Lead strategic planning and implementation of major policy, research and advocacy related initiatives within the Managing Director Office. Develop systems and processes that strengthen knowledge management, organizational learning, and policy coordination. Leadership and People Management (15%) Lead, coach, and develop policy and research staff, consultants, and project teams. Establish work plans, priorities, and performance expectations for direct reports. Foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing team culture. Support workforce planning, recruitment, and professional development within the Policy and Research function. Promote effective collaboration across WES departments to achieve shared organizational objectives.   Your Experience: Required   A bachelor's degree in economics, Public Policy, Political Science, Social Sciences, or another related discipline, or an acceptable equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in economic research or public policy within the social impact, public, or non-profit sectors. Demonstrated technical research capacity, including experience designing and executing applied economic research on immigration and labour markets, from research design and data strategy through analysis, peer review, and publication. Strong econometric and quantitative skills, including regression analysis, causal inference methods, and labour market outcome analysis, with working proficiency in statistical software such as Stata, R, or Python. Minimum five (5) years of management or leadership experience leading teams, consultants, or complex cross-functional initiatives. Demonstrated expertise in Canadian labour market policy, workforce development, credential recognition, immigration or related public policy fields. Experience managing external research partnerships and commissioned research. Experience working with Canadian labour market and immigration data, such as the Longitudinal Immigration Database (IMDB), Census, and Labour Force Survey, including Statistics Canada Research Data Centre or administrative microdata environments. Extensive experience leading policy development, consultation submissions, research projects, and strategic advocacy initiatives. Proven ability to influence policy through research, stakeholder engagement, and strategic partnerships. Experience building and maintaining relationships with senior government officials, business leaders, funders, and sector organizations. Excellent relationship-building skills and executive presence: ability to build strong relationships and work with individuals at all levels of the organization; work collaboratively with people of different backgrounds, experiences, communication styles, and cultures towards collective goals. Strong strategic planning, analytical, and systems thinking capabilities. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive-level briefings, reports, and presentations. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex projects in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment. Excellent judgment, political acuity, and ability to manage sensitive issues with discretion. Knowledge of federal and provincial government decision-making processes. Experience managing external research partnerships and commissioned research. Experience developing organizational policy and advocacy strategies. Desired A record of published economic or policy research, including peer-reviewed publications, working papers, or widely cited policy reports on immigration, economic policy, workforce development, and/or labour market topics. Experience representing an organization publicly through conferences, media, or government consultations. Functional bilingualism in English and French is considered a strong asset.   What We Offer:   Joining our team at WES means embarking on a purpose-driven career with a global impact, where you contribute daily to making a tangible difference in the lives of people worldwide. You'll thrive in an employee-centric environment, with access to learning opportunities, pathways for personal and professional development, and recognition of your achievements. Our inclusive, mission-driven culture values employees and focuses on investing in our people through our culture, people framework, and programming while offering the flexibility of remote work options.
